description: Canonical tool manifest for the FX Pair Analyst template. Skills and commands reference entries by id. Install-on-demand — the agent should install only what a given task requires, not the entire toolkit up-front.

categories.architecture-reference: Patterns borrowed, not integrated as deps

tools.name: fawazahmed0/exchange-api
tools.coverage: 200+ fiat + crypto + metals, daily, ~several years history
tools.use_when: Default free historical spot rates. First choice for daily close series.

tools.name: mphinance/momentum-mcp
tools.install: git clone https://github.com/mphinance/momentum-mcp && cd momentum-mcp && pip install -r requirements.txt
tools.coverage: yfinance-backed: get_historical_data, analyze_technicals (RSI/MACD/SMA/EMA), generate_chart (candlestick PNG), fetch_ticker_news, extract_article. Works for FX via `EURUSD=X` ticker convention.
tools.use_when: Conversational TA lookups and quick chart generation. Good fallback when pandas-ta + plotting feels heavy. Ignore the screen/news tools — equity-biased.

tools.name: stefanoamorelli/fred-mcp-server
tools.coverage: Tools: fred_browse, fred_search, fred_get_series (with transformations pch/pc1/log + frequency aggregation).
tools.use_when: Conversational FRED lookups — browse/search the catalog, fetch a single series with built-in transformations. Use alongside pandas-datareader (`fred` id): MCP for discovery, pandas for bulk merging and quant.

tools.name: LangAlpha macro_mcp_server (lift candidate)
tools.coverage: Treasury yield curve, Fed funds, CPI, economic calendar. FastMCP single-file server, standalone from LangAlpha's runtime (no Daytona/Postgres/Redis). Direct FX rate-differential utility.
tools.use_when: If FRED + pandas-datareader feels insufficient for real-time Treasury/Fed data. Lift the file, swap data_client.fmp for direct FMP HTTP calls, run as a local MCP.

tools.name: tradesdontlie/tradingview-mcp
tools.install: git clone https://github.com/tradesdontlie/tradingview-mcp && cd tradingview-mcp && npm install && node src/server.js
tools.auth: TradingView Desktop subscription; launch app with --remote-debugging-port=9222
tools.coverage: Any symbol TradingView supports — FX pairs included if plan allows. OHLCV via data_get_ohlcv, bar-by-bar replay, chart screenshots, drawing tools, indicator values, Pine Script dev, alerts.
tools.use_when: User has TradingView Desktop and wants chart-anchored analysis — pulling indicator values, annotated screenshots, Pine Script prototyping, or replay-mode backtesting. Preferred for visual/chart workflows over headless fetching.

tools.name: yfinance
tools.coverage: FX pairs via `EURUSD=X` ticker, daily + intraday (limited history)
tools.use_when: Fallback when fawazahmed lacks a cross, or when OHLC (not just close) is needed.

tools.name: alpha_vantage
tools.use_when: Need intraday bars on free tier.

tools.name: oandapyV20
tools.coverage: Broker-grade FX bars/ticks, minute-level historical, live streams
tools.use_when: User has an OANDA account and wants intraday/tick rigor.

tools.name: pandas-datareader (FRED)
tools.coverage: Macro series: DXY, policy rates, inflation, rate differentials, yields
tools.use_when: Always load macro context alongside spot — rate differentials drive majors.

tools.name: Tavily MCP
tools.use_when: Quick news / background lookups. Use for factual retrieval; pair with Perplexity for synthesis.

tools.name: Perplexity
tools.use_when: Synthesized geopolitical briefings tied to a pair and date range. Not for raw rates.

tools.name: pandas-ta
tools.use_when: Default technical indicators — MAs, RSI, MACD, Bollinger, ATR, pivots. Pure Python, no C build.

tools.name: TA-Lib
tools.install: apt install libta-lib0 libta-lib-dev && pip install TA-Lib
tools.use_when: Large indicator batches where pandas-ta is too slow. Otherwise prefer pandas-ta.

tools.name: TuneTA
tools.use_when: Auto-tune indicator parameters per FX pair against a target signal.

tools.name: statsmodels
tools.use_when: ADF stationarity tests, Engle-Granger + Johansen cointegration, VAR, ARIMA. Essential for FX pair analysis.

tools.name: arch
tools.use_when: GARCH/EGARCH/realised-vol modeling. FX vol clusters — use this for vol forecasts.

tools.name: py_vollib
tools.use_when: Black-Scholes greeks + implied vol for FX options.

tools.name: Nixtla statsforecast
tools.use_when: Fast local classical forecasts (AutoARIMA, ETS, Theta). No API key. Default forecaster.

tools.name: Nixtla neuralforecast
tools.use_when: Neural forecasts (NHITS, NBEATS, TFT) when classical is insufficient.

tools.name: Nixtla TimeGPT client
tools.use_when: Zero-shot forecasting baseline. Good for quick 'what does a foundation model expect' sanity check.

tools.name: rateslib
tools.use_when: FX forwards, cross-currency swaps, curve construction, carry analysis.

tools.name: FinancePy
tools.use_when: Exotic FX options, barrier/asian/digital pricing.

tools.name: quantstats
tools.use_when: Default metrics + tearsheet HTML. Feed FX log-returns: Sharpe, Sortino, Calmar, max DD, VaR, CVaR, rolling vol, Monte Carlo.

tools.name: vectorbt
tools.use_when: Vectorised backtest grids — try thousands of indicator-param combos per pair fast.

tools.name: microsoft/qlib
tools.use_when: Serious backtest with IC/Sharpe + factor mining. Heavy — only when simple backtest is insufficient.

tools.name: matplotlib
tools.use_when: Static charts for PDF reports.

tools.name: plotly
tools.use_when: Interactive HTML charts for exploratory analysis.

tools.name: mplfinance
tools.use_when: Candlestick + volume charts, clean defaults.

tools.name: Typst
tools.use_when: Final PDF report generation. Preferred over LaTeX for speed and ergonomics.

tools.name: OpenBB Platform
tools.install: pip install openbb  (base) or pip install 'openbb[all]' (heavy)
tools.use_when: Unified access to many providers (Yahoo, FMP, Polygon, FRED) behind one API. Optional — use when multi-provider fusion matters more than lean deps.

tools.name: JerBouma/FinanceToolkit
tools.use_when: Quick ratio/indicator computations over a ticker — supplements quantstats when dimensional breadth matters.

tools.name: Planning-with-Files (ClarityFinance)
tools.use_when: Multi-phase analyses — use task_plan.md / findings.md / progress.md in context/from-agent/ for long-running workflows.

tools.name: Role-decomposition (FinRobot)
tools.use_when: Split analysis into specialist sub-agents: technical, macro, geopol, flows. Synthesise in final report.

tools.name: Signal-tracker (RKiding Awesome-finance-skills)
tools.use_when: Record each signal with strengthen / weaken / falsify conditions. Update as new data arrives.

tools.name: Programmatic Tool Calling (LangAlpha)
tools.use_when: For quant work: write Python in-session that processes data locally and returns only summary — avoid dumping raw series into context.
